[{"sha":"8c668f3dd3916e96d06131dec97c78a3e62bd0f3","node_id":"C_kwDOAB6-0toAKDhjNjY4ZjNkZDM5MTZlOTZkMDYxMzFkZWM5N2M3OGEzZTYyYmQwZjM","commit":{"author":{"name":"Hubert Boma Manilla","email":"hmanilla@mozilla.com","date":"2026-10-12T09:32:45Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-10-12T09:32:45Z"},"message":"Infrastructure and build tooling upgrade (#537)

* Build lib/mappings.wasm with wasm-pack and wasm-bindgen

The previous build pipeline could not be run at all on a current Rust
toolchain. Three of its four tools failed outright:

  - cargo build: `undefined symbol: mapping_callback`, because the import
    blocks lacked `#[link(wasm_import_module = "env")]` and modern rust-lld
    rejects undefined symbols
  - wasm-gc 0.1.6: `InvalidTableReference(128)`
  - wasm-nm (which drives wasm-snip): `Not an unsigned 1-bit integer: 128`

Only wasm-opt still worked, so the committed binary was not reproducible
from its own sources. CI never noticed because the `wasm` job only ran a
bare `cargo build` and never exercised build.py.

Replace build.py and who-calls.py with build.sh, which drives wasm-pack.
wasm-pack vendors its own wasm-bindgen and wasm-opt, reducing the four
hand-installed binaries to one. Two targets are built, selected by the
existing package.json#browser field: `nodejs` for CommonJS and `web` for
browsers. Both emit the same .wasm; build.sh asserts this. The shipped
filename stays lib/mappings.wasm so URLs passed to
SourceMapConsumer.initialize keep working.

Port the ABI to wasm-bindgen. allocate_mappings, parse_mappings,
free_mappings and get_last_error collapse into parseMappings() plus a
generated free(), so JS no longer hand-manages a buffer or memcpys into
exports.memory.buffer. Callbacks are passed per-call, which removes the
callbackStack and withMappingCallback machinery. Mapping construction
stays in JS to keep every mapping on one hidden class.

Note that a JS exception thrown from a mapping callback unwinds through
the wasm frame and skips Rust's borrow guard, leaving the handle
permanently borrowed so that free() then fails. The callback boundary is
therefore declared `catch` and every query method returns
Result<(), JsValue>, releasing the borrow before the exception
propagates. Any future &mut self method that calls into JS needs the
same treatment.

Also drop the unused `rand` dependency, turn off `debug` in
[profile.release] (it was responsible for 1.6 MB of debuginfo in a
shipped artifact), and set opt-level="z", lto, codegen-units=1 and
panic="abort". lib/mappings.wasm goes from 48,526 to 28,556 bytes.

Commit both Cargo.lock files, pin the toolchain in rust-toolchain.toml,
and add a `wasm-dist` CI job that rebuilds the committed artifacts and
fails if they differ byte-for-byte. Verified that the job exits non-zero
when the Rust sources drift.

Bump eslint's ecmaVersion to 2020 for the dynamic import() in
read-wasm-browser.js, and keep the generated glue out of eslint --fix and
prettier so neither rewrites it and breaks the byte comparison.

* Strip import.meta.url from the generated browser glue

`import.meta` is a hard parse error in webpack 4 and other pre-2020
bundlers:

    ERROR in ./lib/mappings-glue-browser.mjs 336:56
    Module parse failed: Unexpected token (336:56)
    >         module_or_path = new URL('mappings.wasm', import.meta.url);

This broke `npm run build` in bench/, and would equally break any
consumer of this package that bundles with webpack 4.

The branch it appears in is unreachable here: read-wasm-browser.js
validates its input and always passes the URL or bytes explicitly, so
`module_or_path` is never undefined. Replace it at build time with a
throw carrying the same message read-wasm-browser.js uses, and extend
build.sh's post-build guard to assert no `import.meta` survives.

* Drop the dead 'url' core module fallback in lib/url.js

`lib/url.js` fell back to `require("url").URL` when `URL` was not a
global, which was only the case on Node 8. This package requires Node
>= 12 and `URL` has been global since Node 10, so the fallback was
unreachable.

It was not harmless, though: bundlers that no longer polyfill Node core
modules fail outright on it. Under webpack 5 this breaks `npm run build`
in bench/ with:

    Module not found: Error: Can't resolve 'url' in '.../lib'
    BREAKING CHANGE: webpack < 5 used to include polyfills for node.js
    core modules by default.

The comment above it also claimed the file was overridden via
`package.json#browser` to use `lib/url-browser.js`. That stopped being
true in b95ecf0, which removed `lib/url-browser.js` without removing the
browser mapping's last reader or this comment.

* Upgrade the benchmark bundler to webpack 5

webpack 4 could not parse the `import.meta.url` that wasm-bindgen emits
into the browser glue. That specific blocker is gone now that build.sh
strips it, but webpack 4 is six years old and its webpack-cli 3 pairing
is long unmaintained, so move the benchmark to webpack 5.

The upgrade surfaced one real bug in the library, fixed separately in
64191de: webpack 5 no longer polyfills Node core modules, which exposed
a dead `require("url")` fallback in lib/url.js.

Commit a lockfile as well. The benchmark had none, so `npm install` here
previously resolved whatever was current, which is how the webpack 4
tree drifted far enough to break in the first place.

* Do not track a lockfile for the benchmark

Reverts the lockfile added in ba82cf4. The benchmark is a private,
non-published helper and was never intended to pin its own dependency
tree; `package.json`'s ranges are enough for it.

* Install wasm-pack directly instead of via jetli/wasm-pack-action

Download the official v0.15.0 release binary and verify it against a
pinned SHA-256, so the reproducibility check doesn't depend on a
third-party action.

* Require Node.js 18 or later

The wasm-pack-built lib/mappings.wasm uses WebAssembly multi-value and
reference types, which Node.js 12, 14 and 16 cannot load. Bump
engines.node to >= 18 and test on Node 18, 20 and 22 in CI.

* Run the Rust CI matrix on its intended toolchains

wasm-mappings/rust-toolchain.toml pins stable 1.98.1, and rustup prefers
it over the directory override actions-rs sets on the repo root. As a
result every matrix job ran on 1.98.1, and the nightly-only benches
failed with "#![feature] may not be used on the stable release channel".

Set RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN from the matrix in CI, default the bench job to
nightly when run locally, and correct the toolchain file's comment.

* Pin binaryen 132 for the reproducible wasm build

wasm-pack uses a wasm-opt from PATH when there is one and otherwise
downloads its own (binaryen 117 for wasm-pack 0.15.0). The committed
lib/mappings.wasm was optimized with binaryen 132, so the wasm-dist CI
job, which has no system wasm-opt, produced different bytes and failed.

Make build.sh require binaryen 132 on PATH, install that release in CI
(verified against a pinned SHA-256), and document the requirement in
CONTRIBUTING.md.

* Run ci/script.sh from wasm-mappings/ regardless of the caller's cwd

The script relied on CI's working-directory default. Run from the repo
root, the wasm-dist job failed with "./build.sh: No such file or
directory", and rustup did not pick up wasm-mappings/rust-toolchain.toml.

* Move source-map-mappings to Rust edition 2024

Set `edition` in [package] (under [profile.release] Cargo ignored it and
the crate stayed on 2015), name the anonymous parameters in
ComparatorFunction::compare, and use `dyn Iterator` in the quickcheck
tests. lib/mappings.wasm is byte-for-byte unchanged.

* Fix cargo warnings in the wasm-mappings crates

- Drop the deprecated std::u32 / std::i64 module imports.
- Assign instead of discarding a mem::replace result.
- Store the never-read observer as PhantomData<O>.
- Spell out elided lifetimes in two return types.
- Upgrade quickcheck 0.5 -> 1.1 (0.5 trips a future-incompat warning)
  and port the Arbitrary impls to the 1.x API.
- Set edition 2024 on source-map-mappings-wasm-api, which had none.

The source changes alter codegen slightly, so lib/mappings.wasm is
rebuilt (28556 -> 28563 bytes) with the pinned toolchain and binaryen.

* Disable the byte comparison in the wasm-dist CI job

The job still rebuilds lib/mappings.wasm and its glue, but no longer
fails when the result differs from the committed artifacts.

* Re-enable the wasm-dist byte comparison for lib/mappings.wasm

Partially undoes dd28c67: CI again fails if rebuilding from source does
not reproduce the committed lib/mappings.wasm. The generated glue files
remain unchecked.

* Check the generated glue files in wasm-dist again

Restores the byte comparison for lib/mappings-glue.js, .d.ts and the
browser .mjs/.d.mts alongside lib/mappings.wasm, so ci/script.sh is back
to how it was before dd28c67.

* Remap source paths so the wasm build is machine-independent

Panic locations embed absolute source paths in lib/mappings.wasm, which
differ between machines (checkout location, $CARGO_HOME, and whether
rustup's rust-src is installed). A build on macOS was 28563 bytes while
GitHub CI produced 28471, failing the wasm-dist check. Pass
--remap-path-prefix for each so the paths are fixed, and rebuild
lib/mappings.wasm (now 28443 bytes). trim-paths would do this but is not
stable in Cargo 1.98.1.

* Update docs and comments for the Node.js 18 requirement

Bump the Node.js version in CONTRIBUTING.md and the lib/url.js comment
to 18, and use .catch() in read-wasm-browser.js.

* Bring the contributing docs up to date

- Drop the `npm run build` / dist/source-map.js instructions; there is
  no JS build step since dist/ was removed in #362.
- Refresh the sample `npm test` output.
- Pin wasm-pack 0.15.0 in the install command, matching CI.
- Document the binaryen 132 requirement in wasm-mappings/CONTRIBUTING.md,
  which still claimed wasm-pack was the only tool needed.
- Point wasm-pack links at wasm-bindgen.github.io; the rustwasm.github.io
  page is gone.
